category_title: Struggling readers supported by literal comprehension scaffolding
minimal_context: The student and teacher are discussing a self-selected book about a pancake eating contest during a one-on-one reading conference.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's discuss your book. What happened during the pancake eating contest?

STUDENT: He wanted to eat the most pancakes.

TUTOR: What did he do with the juice?

STUDENT: He didn’t know that they could drink a lot of juice, more than him.

TUTOR: How would you describe the way the character acted when he did that?

STUDENT: They were silly.

options.A: Ask a series of inference and justified follow-up questions (e.g., "What did he do in the story that makes you think he was silly?", "Why do you think he had them drink the juice on purpose?").
options.B: Allow the student to change aspects of the text, such as the font size and background lighting, on an e-reader during the reading conference.
options.C: Provide a break card on the desk as a prompt for the student to take a break from the reading conference when needed by holding up the card.
options.D: Segment the reading conference and the discussion of the self-selected book about the pancake eating contest into shorter time periods.
